beats.subline: Friday, November 6, 2026 close — the Nasdaq and S&P 500 rebounded from Thursday's AI-chip selloff while the Dow slipped, closing out a losing week for stocks.
beats.body: Chip and AI-infrastructure names that led Thursday's rout, including Nvidia and Micron, bounced back Friday, but the Dow lagged as investors kept weighing the prior session's correction; all three indexes still finished the week lower.

beats.headline: Taiwan logs 11 PLA aircraft, nine crossing the Strait median line, in a single day
beats.body: Taiwan's Ministry of National Defense reported 11 Chinese military aircraft, 10 naval vessels and three official ships operating around the island in the 24 hours to Saturday morning, with nine of the aircraft sorties crossing the Taiwan Strait median line.

beats.headline: Trump confirms new 'minor' US strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island as diplomacy continues
beats.body: Trump said US forces carried out fresh, limited strikes on Iranian air defenses on Qeshm Island near the Strait of Hormuz, the first action since Tuesday's midterms, while saying he has no immediate plan for a broader campaign and that Qatar-mediated talks with Tehran are continuing.

beats.headline: Anthropic adds beta 'project tags' so Claude Enterprise customers can track AI spend by cost code
beats.body: The November 6 beta feature lets eligible Claude Enterprise organizations tag projects with codes they already use, such as charge codes or client-matter numbers, so spend generated inside those projects can be viewed, exported, or pulled via the Analytics API by tag.

beats.headline: Bears injury report: Monangai and two cornerbacks questionable for Bucs, Benedet and Jarrett back to full
beats.body: Running back Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) was upgraded to limited practice after missing the last two games, while cornerbacks Malik Muhammad (toe) and Tyrique Stevenson (thumb) are questionable for Sunday night's game against Tampa Bay; left tackle Theo Benedet and defensive tackle Grady Jarrett both practiced fully all week after being limited by shoulder and groin injuries.
